notes.text: Pavel Dorofeyev is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Will Cuylle has taken his spot beside J.T. Miller and Tye Kartye.
Oliver Bjorkstrand is out 2-3 months (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game.

Sean Durzi is day to day and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 117:15 together, up from 45% with Durzi.
Glenn Gawdin was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Eeli Tolvanen and Jaroslav Chmelař.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.
Konsta Helenius is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 10 games.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 7% last season.

stakes: The Rangers go in third in the Metropolitan with 27 points, the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic with 22 points.

story.head: Carrick meets his old team
paras: The Sabres (9-9-4) beat Washington 6-3 on Thursday, and the Rangers have won three straight. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 20th).

This season, the Rangers have outscored teams 67-58, but only 42-40 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 15-9. This season, the Sabres have been outscored 76-64, but only 46-43 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 23-13.

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). As for the Sabres, they rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage against the Sabres’ penalty kill (25th). Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Adam Fox (2 G / 22 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 22 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (14 G / 10 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jack Quinn (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.

the Rangers has two options in net: Dylan Garand (7-7-1 / .910 SV% in 13 GS) and Joonas Korpisalo (3-0-0 / .940 SV% in 3 GS). Garand has started six of their last ten games, so expect him back in net after Korpisalo got the last one on Nov 16. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (6-4-3 / .872 SV% in 12 GS) and Alex Lyon (0-2-1 / .898 SV% in 3 GS). Luukkonen has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: Sam Carrick faces the Rangers for the first time since leaving.
The Rangers are newly without Pavel Dorofeyev and Oliver Bjorkstrand, and have been without Igor Shesterkin and Sean Durzi for several games.
J.T. Miller has a point in six straight games against Buffalo.
The Sabres have been without Konsta Helenius since Oct 27.
